assumptions: The launch plan covers a defined geography and brand set for which independent or authorized technicians can lawfully perform the promised work.
Any response entitlement is contractually bounded and is not represented as insurance or an unconditional repair guarantee.
The family installation business provides only consensual introductions and does not transfer customer relationships or data without permission.
Annual plan funds can be reserved sufficiently to honor refunds, included visits, and peak-season contractor commitments.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Signed seasonal capacity terms from multiple qualified technicians; warranty-validity confirmation by covered brand; local installed-base and wait-time data; at least twenty paid homeowner plans; measured travel, visit, support, cancellation, repeat-visit, and callout costs; renewal intent; and a stress-tested peak-week service-level model.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Pre-reserving qualified technician capacity addresses the supply bottleneck that a lead directory does not, particularly when heating failures peak seasonally. The insight is credible but not yet supported by measured regional wait times, technician idle-period preferences, or evidence that independent capacity can preserve brand-specific warranty requirements.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Maintenance is already a visible paid event, Bosch cites roughly 1,000 PLN annual maintenance cost for most systems, and winter downtime can be costly and urgent. Willingness to prepay 1,200-1,800 PLN for a multi-brand independent plan, rather than buy an authorized visit when needed, is untested and urgency is weaker where annual service is not legally or contractually required.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Annual prepayment can finance capacity reservations and make cash conversion attractive. At the proposed price, an underlying maintenance visit near 1,000 PLN leaves limited room for acquisition, travel, remote triage, scheduling, support, reserves, repeat visits, and discounted callouts; contribution margin and winter claim incidence are unknown.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: A growing, long-lived heat-pump installed base creates recurring aftercare demand, and one geography plus a limited brand set is a sensible initial scope. The candidate does not quantify local installed-base density, systems outside dependable authorized coverage, service wait times, brand mix, or enough annual plan demand to create efficient routes.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Multi-brand portability and transparent response performance could help owners whose original installer is unavailable. Bosch alone reports a nationwide organization of more than 500 authorized technicians with parts, training, dispatch, and warranty ties, illustrating the control and bundling power of OEMs alongside installers, utilities, and insurers.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: The model could add geographies, brands, property-manager portfolios, remote triage, and adjacent heating equipment. Each geography requires sufficient route density and dependable local capacity, each brand can require authorization and parts knowledge, and physical fulfillment makes expansion operationally heavier than pure software.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Density, technician performance data, fault histories, parts patterns, and seasonal reservations could improve routing and first-visit resolution over time. The proposed reservations are nonexclusive and unsigned, technicians are replaceable but scarce, customer contracts renew annually, and incumbents already possess richer brand-specific service data and networks.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The family installation business offers a lawful way to observe handoffs and seek opt-in referrals, while the founder's analytics skills fit scheduling and triage. It supplies no secured homeowner book, technician capacity, manufacturer authorization, parts access, or service-level rights, so the venture begins without control of fulfillment.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Heat-pump deployment is creating a progressively larger aftercare base, and each installed unit has a 15-20 year expected operating horizon according to the cited manufacturer material. The candidate has not shown that current Polish service scarcity is worsening or that owners are moving away from incumbent authorized networks now.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Installer handoff, annual-service timing, property-manager portfolios, local intent search, and a family-firm pilot are concrete routes closely aligned with the purchase trigger. Original installers and manufacturers may protect their customer and warranty relationships, and no attachment rate, referral term, or acquisition cost is evidenced.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The physical work can be outsourced and planned maintenance can begin without promising emergency coverage. Reliable winter response requires live scheduling, contractor quality control, parts availability, consumer-safe plan wording, refunds and reserves, documentation acceptable to manufacturers, and liability management; scarcity raises both failure risk and cost at the exact moment demand peaks.

highest_value_structural_change: Start as a pre-season planned-maintenance membership for one dense geography and limited authorized brands, with no guaranteed emergency repair; secure prepaid minimum-volume technician blocks at fixed prices and add response guarantees only after observed utilization and first-visit-resolution economics support them.
main_structural_strength: Prepaid homeowner demand can be matched with contracted seasonal technician slots, creating a tangible service entitlement and a potential density-and-performance learning loop rather than merely brokering leads.
primary_score_limiter: No technician reservation price, local capacity commitment, callout frequency, route density, or homeowner prepayment evidence shows that the plan can deliver a credible winter entitlement at a positive fully loaded margin.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: A major manufacturer already combines a nationwide authorized network, original parts, training, quality control, diagnosis tools, and warranty-linked service, while the cited maintenance cost is close enough to the proposed plan price to leave little room for an independent intermediary's full cost stack.
